title: FlashAttention prefetch-shard adaptor and degradation mitigation investigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Since integrating FlashAttention v3 builds selectively for some model classes, we've observed intermittent decoding latency spikes and OOMs for long-context mixed-precision workloads during prefill -> decode handoff. Behavior is more frequent on multi-tenant Dedicated hosts where microbatch sizes vary. This ticket investigates root causes and implements a pragmatic adaptor that prefetches and shards KV workspace reservations to avoid catastrophic kernel selection regressions.

Observed symptoms: p95 decode latency jumps (x2-x5) on 2048+ contexts; occasional CUDA OOMs during concurrent prefill + decode on same GPU; increased variance in kernel choice selector for sequences > 1024 tokens leading to suboptimal FlashAttention variant chosen.

Hypothesis: The kernel selector's heuristics assume worst-case contiguous workspace availability. On mixed workloads the runtime fast-path picks v3 kernels that require a larger transient workspace. When prefill and decode overlap the allocator fragments the workspace and the kernel falls back late into a slower variant or triggers OOM. Combined with our continuous-batching and prefetch pipeline, this causes jitter and degradation.

Goal: 1) Reproduce reliably in an isolated microbench 2) Add a prefetch-shard adaptor that reserves and fragments workspace before kernel selection to make choice deterministic 3) Add staged rollback/canary and perf guardrails so hosted/dedicated users see minimal disruption.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repro case that fails > 90% of runs before fix and succeeds > 95% after fix on same hardware images.
- p95 decode latency reduction on target long-context benchmark: from 540ms -> <= 260ms (measured on p4d.24xlarge analog).
- No increase in memory tail OOMs during 1h soak at 16 concurrent workers.

Notes on scope: This is a runtime-level mitigation; a later follow-up ticket will implement kernel autotuning table updates and a permanent scheduler change if necessary.
steps_to_reproduce: Checkout runtime branch: git checkout feature/flashattn-prefetch-adaptor
Observe: run sample 10 times; prior to fix expect 6/10 runs with p95 > 500ms or OOMs; after fix expect < 2/10 failures
benchmarks: Baseline (before): throughput=125 tokens/sec, p50=62ms, p95=540ms on p4-sim; OOM rate ~6% over 100 runs
After prefetch-shard adaptor (local dev): throughput=160 tokens/sec, p50=58ms, p95=240ms; OOM rate 0/100
Canary (small fleet): throughput change +18%, p95 stable at ~250ms over 6h soak
proposed_approach: Add a prefetch-shard adaptor layer between allocator and kernel selector that: probes required transient workspace for candidate kernels, reserves fragmented slices of workspace (shards) for prefill and decode paths, and guarantees deterministic kernel selection based on reserved shards.
Introduce a soft reservation API for workspace that falls back to conservative kernels when total free contiguous workspace < threshold.
Instrument allocator telemetry (fragmentation ratio, failed reservations) and add eviction counters to monitor in console dashboards.
Staged rollout: dev -> perf-canary -> dedicated canary -> global. Feature flag gate with fallback=true option to allow automatic rollback to prior behaviour if SLOs degrade.
decision_log: 2026-02-23: Decided to implement adaptor shim instead of changing kernel implementations to keep integration risk low (Aisha/Marco/Jing).
2026-03-02: Chose deterministic shard reservation over greedy coalescing to prioritize stability for Dedicated tenants (engineering sync).
2026-03-10: Agreed to expose allocator fragmentation metrics in Console and add an automatic canary guard that rejects rollout if fragmentation ratio > 0.45 over 10m windows.
implementation_notes: Adapter lives in runtime/allocator/prefetch_shard_adaptor.cc and exposes C++ API reserve_shards(vector<size_t> shards) — unit tests should mock CUDA allocator.
Feature flag: runtime.prefetch_shard_adaptor.enabled (default=false); rollout controlled by release manager.
Add unit + integration tests under tests/allocator/test_prefetch_shard_adaptor.py and e2e bench harness in infra/benchmarks/long_context_with_overlap.py
Update kernel selector scoring to consider reserved_shard_count and reserved_contiguous_bytes as tie-breakers.
Backwards compatibility: adaptor must gracefully no-op when flashattn v3 not available; will fall back to existing selection heuristics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Additional reservation overhead could reduce peak throughput. Mitigation: soft reservation path that releases shards if utilization is low and falls back to coalesced allocation after prefill completes.

Risk: Uncovered edge-case where reserved shards still produce fragmentation for very large models. Mitigation: guardrail to pin kernel version to v2 for problematic model classes via model manifest until autotuner is improved.
Risk: Rollout might trigger regressions on older GPU drivers. Mitigation: driver compatibility matrix check in canary and automatic disable on failed driver profiles.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (dev): Merge to feature branch behind flag; run full unit and integration suite (automatic).
Step 2 (perf-canary): Deploy to 4 canary hosts running long-context soak for 48h, monitor p95, OOMs, fragmentation metrics. Threshold to proceed: no p95 regression and OOM count unchanged.
Step 3 (dedicated-canary): Enable for 2 small Dedicated customers (consent obtained) for 1 week with SLA guardrails.
Step 4: Global staged rollout across Dedicated and Hosted; monitor for 72h with automatic rollback if fragmentation ratio spikes or p95 increases > 15%.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Add long_context_prefill board showing p50/p95 for prefill and decode, OOM rate, fragmentation ratio
Alerts: p95_decode > baseline * 1.25 for 5m; OOM_rate > 0.5% over 10m; failed_reservations > 3/min
